leakage.note: Without-time runs put serum_sodium in the place of time; the folds are the same 15 repeated 5-fold splits.

diff.before: Regulatory-aware clinical pipeline: evaluates cohort with follow-up time. Benchmark demonstrated that time inflates MCC scores significantly across both quantum and classical baselines.
diff.after: This run includes follow-up time, which the track permits. Follow-up time can carry outcome information and would not be available at true prediction time, so reported MCC may be higher than for a deployable model. No no-time comparison is included in this file.
Angle Embedding fidelity kernel (product-state, no entanglement)

diff.before: Validation benchmark completed. Follows regulatory guidelines reporting confidence intervals and rigorous holdout metrics.
diff.after: QSVM holdout MCC is comparable to the classical models. Its 5-fold CV MCC is lower than RandomForest's, but the difference is not statistically significant (p = 0.112).

withtime.protocol: 5-fold stratified x 3 repeats = 15 paired splits on the 239 training patients (seed 1)

mcc.sentence: Observed MCC delta of +0.0009 between qsvm_zz_x0.3 (0.5999) and xgboost (0.5990) with bootstrap 95% CI [-0.0611, +0.0653] and Nadeau-Bengio corrected p = 1.0000 across 3 quantum configurations does not reject the null hypothesis at threshold 0.02. No conclusive advantage demonstrated.

auroc.sentence: Observed AUROC delta of -0.0299 between qsvm_zz_x0.3 (0.8744) and random_forest (0.9042) with bootstrap 95% CI [-0.0519, -0.0052] and Nadeau-Bengio corrected p = 0.5836 across 3 quantum configurations does not reject the null hypothesis at threshold 0.02. No conclusive advantage demonstrated.

notime.protocol: 5-fold stratified x 3 repeats = 15 paired splits on the 239 training patients (seed 1)

mcc.sentence: Observed MCC delta of -0.0028 between qsvm_zz_x1.0 (0.4137) and random_forest (0.4165) with bootstrap 95% CI [-0.0460, +0.0426] and Nadeau-Bengio corrected p = 1.0000 across 3 quantum configurations does not reject the null hypothesis at threshold 0.02. No conclusive advantage demonstrated.

auroc.sentence: Observed AUROC delta of +0.0035 between qsvm_zz_x0.3 (0.7906) and random_forest (0.7871) with bootstrap 95% CI [-0.0173, +0.0277] and Nadeau-Bengio corrected p = 1.0000 across 3 quantum configurations does not reject the null hypothesis at threshold 0.02. No conclusive advantage demonstrated.

claims.claim: E1 (Bloq, ZZ default): MCC 0.0000; 0 of 48 patients predicted to die.
claims.recomputed: MCC recomputed from the platform confusion matrix [[33, 0], [15, 0]]: 0.0000; accuracy 0.6875.
claims.evidence: Arithmetic on the raw platform output. This checks the report's reading of the file, not the platform's run.

claims.claim: E2 (Bloq, ZZ default): MCC 0.0116; 3 of 48 patients predicted to die.
claims.recomputed: MCC recomputed from the platform confusion matrix [[31, 2], [14, 1]]: 0.0116; accuracy 0.6667.
claims.evidence: Arithmetic on the raw platform output. This checks the report's reading of the file, not the platform's run.

claims.claim: Stratified split: 239 training and 60 test patients with matching death rates.
claims.recomputed: 239 train (death rate 0.322), 60 test (death rate 0.317, 19 deaths).
claims.evidence: Counted from the bundled CSVs.

claims.claim: Test rows fall slightly outside [0, 1] because the scaler only saw training rows.
claims.recomputed: Test feature minimum -0.094, maximum 1.047. The study clips test rows to [0, 1] before encoding.
claims.evidence: Min and max over both test files.

claims.claim: E3: wider input range and deeper circuits hurt the ZZ kernel (8 rows of the report table).
claims.recomputed: 8 of 8 rows match to the report's two decimals. Example: withtime range 0 to 1 depth 1 gives CV 0.5190 and test 0.6716.
claims.evidence: The report calls these approximate. They are now exact.

claims.claim: E4: shrinking the input range to 0.3 helped the with-time data (CV 0.60, test 0.81).
claims.recomputed: 4 of 4 cells match. With time: range 0.3 CV 0.5999 / test 0.8055; range 1.0 CV 0.5377 / test 0.6716.
claims.evidence: Min-max rows only.

claims.claim: The range 0.3 was chosen on cross-validation, not on the holdout.
claims.recomputed: Across five ranges (with time) CV MCC varies by 0.076 but holdout MCC varies by 0.162.
claims.evidence: Holdout MCC on 60 patients is noisy, so choosing a range by holdout would mostly choose noise.

claims.claim: E5 QSVM holdout: MCC 0.746, accuracy 0.883, recall 0.895, confusion [[36, 5], [2, 17]].
claims.recomputed: Independent angle-embedding kernel gives MCC 0.745976, accuracy 0.8833, confusion [[36, 5], [2, 17]]. ROC-AUC 0.9345 against 0.9332 submitted (score function differs).
claims.evidence: All five class-prediction metrics match to 9 decimals. Only the score-based ROC-AUC differs.

claims.recomputed: 4 of 5 folds match. Mean 0.5036 against 0.5068. Fold 4: 0.6167 against 0.6325.
claims.evidence: Same folds (5-fold, shuffled, seed 42). The fold 4 gap is 0.016 MCC and its cause is not known.

claims.claim: The submitted kernel is an angle-embedding fidelity kernel with no entanglement, not a ZZ feature map.
claims.recomputed: The product-state kernel reproduces the submitted holdout exactly (MCC 0.746). A true ZZ kernel at the same range gives holdout MCC 0.672.
claims.evidence: Two kernels, one match. The platform's own export called it ZZFeatureMap, which the corrected file no longer does.

claims.claim: In E5 logistic regression predicted the majority class in every fold (CV MCC 0.000, holdout 0.191).
claims.recomputed: Reproduced when the inputs are multiplied by 0.3: CV 0.0000, holdout 0.1912. On the full 0 to 1 range the same model gets CV 0.5483 and holdout 0.7460, which equals the QSVM's holdout MCC.
claims.evidence: Inferred recipe. The collapse is a regularisation effect of shrunken inputs, so beating this baseline says little.

claims.claim: E5 SVM-RBF baseline: CV MCC 0.525, holdout 0.779.
claims.evidence: scikit-learn SVC defaults on the same folds.

claims.claim: E5 RandomForest, GradientBoosting and XGBoost baseline numbers.
claims.recomputed: RandomForest: CV 0.6074 vs 0.6291, holdout 0.6806 vs 0.7785; GradientBoosting: CV 0.5876 vs 0.5752, holdout 0.7328 vs 0.7785; XGBoost: CV 0.5775 vs 0.6112, holdout 0.6321 vs 0.6559
claims.evidence: Default settings and seed 42 do not reproduce them. The platform's tree settings are not visible to us.

claims.claim: QSVM vs RandomForest paired on E5 folds: delta MCC -0.122, 95% CI [-0.290, 0.045], p = 0.112.
claims.evidence: Plain paired t-test on 5 folds. The guard's corrected test (below) is stricter.

claims.claim: E6 local ZZ benchmark (not submitted): QSVM CV MCC 0.569, holdout 0.806.
claims.recomputed: Fresh run against the stored file: 0 differing values (timing excluded). QSVM CV 0.5688, holdout 0.8055.
claims.evidence: Every metric and fold score identical.

claims.claim: The submitted file differs from the original Bloq-pipeline export in three text fields only.
claims.recomputed: 3 fields differ: /metadata/leakage_audit_note, /metadata/quantum_configuration/feature_map, /statistical_comparison/verdict. Every number is identical.
claims.evidence: Programmatic recursive diff of the two JSON files.

claims.claim: Follow-up time carries outcome information, so with-time scores are optimistic for a deployable model.
claims.source: docs/MORPHOS_REPORT_AND_PRD.md, risks; no no-time comparison was in the submitted file
claims.recomputed: `time` alone has AUROC 0.812, higher than any other single feature (best other: serum_creatinine 0.753). Swapping it for serum_sodium changes CV MCC by: QSVM +0.204, SVM-RBF +0.195, LogisticRegression +0.229, RandomForest +0.164.
claims.evidence: Local repeated-CV run, same 15 splits for both feature sets. Not run on Bloq.

claims.claim: The Bloq E1 and E2 collapse is explained by kernel concentration at large input ranges (report, E3).
claims.recomputed: Local ZZ kernels on 0 to 1 inputs never predicted 'no deaths' in 300 random 191/48 splits (no-time: 0, with-time: 0), and MCC was at most 0.05 in 0.3% of no-time splits. Local collapse appears only at range 0 to 2pi.
claims.evidence: Split luck does not explain E1 and E2. Whether the platform rescales inputs internally cannot be checked from outside.

claims.claim: On a 60-patient holdout, one or two patients move MCC noticeably.
claims.source: holdout confusion matrix of the E5 QSVM
claims.recomputed: Baseline 0.746. One prediction flipped: 0.702 to 0.790. Two flipped: 0.659 to 0.834.
claims.evidence: Computed from the four confusion-matrix counts.

claims.claim: E5 was produced by the Bloq platform pipeline.
claims.recomputed: No platform signature or run identifier in the file can be checked from outside Bloq.
claims.evidence: This tool signs and hashes what you hand it. It cannot attest to where a number came from. Keep the platform screenshots and the experiment ids.
